n.quote:
A reasonable alternative was implemented instead, with all analyses based on six
participating teacher-student dyads, couched within a nonconcurrent (with respect to the study’s chronological time frame) MBD and
associated randomization-test analyses. ... Each of the seven eligible students gave oral assent for participation. As noted previously, one student withdrew his assent to
   participate in outcome assessment. This withdrawal resulted in having complete data for six (4 boys and 2 girls) students.

WCPM from baseline (M = 59.3) to intervention (M = 72.0), p = .006. ... A randomization test conducted on these data revealed a statistically significant change in level across students following the
introduction of the intervention (p = .001), from a baseline mean of 60.0 WCPM to an intervention mean of 91.2. ... nificant increase in frequency of engaged behavior (p = .001), from an average of 63% engagement during baseline to 82% during ... There was a statistically

intervention.

notes:
Assigned fields only: n_o, es_value_o, pval_value_o. The supplied original locator p.26 does not exist in the supplied 19-page published version. The description names reading and behavior collectively and does not identify a particular outcome/test. No mapping from manuscript pagination is supplied. Standard passages, training passages, engaged behavior, and disruptive behavior are distinct candidate primary outcomes; they cannot be assigned to this row by row order or numerical values. Candidate primary effect sizes as printed: standard reading passages d=1.33, g=1.21, adjusted NAP=0.57 (p. 12); training reading passages d=2.80, g=2.53, adjusted NAP=0.94 (p. 13); engaged behavior d=1.14, g=1.03, adjusted NAP=0.55 (p. 15); disruptive behavior d=− 0.85, g=− 0.76, adjusted NAP=0.50 (p. 15). Candidate randomization p values: standard reading .006, training reading .001, engaged behavior .001, disruptive behavior .001, all printed equalities. These are not assigned values. The source expressly distinguishes summary effect sizes from structured omnibus randomization tests (p. 12): It is important to note that the summary statistics are based on a general comparison of students’ A- and B-phase observations, which
are not directly connected to the structured omnibus multiple-baseline randomization test that was conducted. Candidate model N=6 is explicitly stated, with six complete student cases; no arithmetic derived and no row-specific N committed. Secondary GAS outcomes also report d values rather than g (p. 15). Source identity verified from title/authors/DOI on p. 1. No PDF supplied, so no PDF rendering/layout verification was possible. Unassigned replication and success fields are placeholders.
